_why: This file was a BOOTSTRAP MANIFEST generated 2026-07-04, hand-authored from agents/*.md front-matter — eleven days before git-teammates existed (super-agents/ landed 2026-07-15). It could not describe the current fleet because the architecture it described predates it. roster.json was then built 2026-07-24 as the canonical combined roster of the ENTIRE fleet, which left TWO files both claiming canonical. Michael's ruling 2026-07-25: ONE documented source. That is roster.json.
_also: By 2026-07-25 this file had grown to ~29KB and could not be read back whole by ANY path — base64 inflated it past the ~30KB blob-API cap, and the raw path served a cache-frozen ~10KB copy instead of the real blob. It was therefore unreadable, unverifiable, and unsafe to rewrite. A source of truth nobody can open is not a source of truth. Its full pre-retirement content is preserved in git history at the commit before this stub.

_where_its_contents_went.lens role text: agents/<slug>.md front-matter — which THIS file's own header already called canonical
_where_its_contents_went.domain_procedures[]: the AI Toolkit index Quick-Scan trigger table
_where_its_contents_went.changelog: git history + PR descriptions (already the standing rule: what-changed history is git + PR, never an inline changelog)

There is no pair anymore, so there is no sync obligation: update roster.json, and keep the AI Toolkit index's behavioral trigger rows current. Do not resurrect a second manifest to 'mirror' the roster — that duplication is exactly what was retired here.
_do_not: Do not regenerate, extend, or read this file as fleet data. If something still points here, repoint it at roster.json. Kept as a loud stub rather than deleted so a stale pointer fails visibly instead of silently serving a 2026-07-04 view of the world.
